label: Burlina

names.text: "Bassanese", "Binda", "Boccarda" and "Pezzata degli altipiani" from the Wikipedia article's alternative-names line.

about.text: A small, horned, pied black-and-white traditional breed from the mountainous Veneto region of north-east Italy, mainly in the provinces of Treviso, Verona and Vicenza. It is dual-purpose but raised principally for milk. Its milk is higher in kappa-casein than Friesian milk, which makes it suited to cheese-making, including Morlacco del Grappa.

sources.text: Wikipedia article: "the mountainous areas of the Veneto region" in north-east Italy, distribution mainly in Treviso, Verona and Vicenza; "a dual-purpose breed" but "raised principally for milk production"; coat pied black-and-white and horned; milk higher in kappa-casein and more suitable for cheese-making; milk traditionally used for Morlacco del Grappa.

origin.place: The mountainous areas of the Veneto region, north-east Italy.

sources.text: Wikipedia article: "the mountainous areas of the Veneto region"; the article also says "The origins of the Burlina are unknown", so no date of formation is given.
Wikipedia article, citing Bigi & Zanon (2008): 11,283 in the Veneto in 1956. The figure is for the Veneto region, not the whole of Italy.
Wikipedia article, citing Bigi & Zanon (2008): "about 300" in the Veneto in 2008. The article's figure is approximate, and the count is for the Veneto region, not the whole of Italy.
Wikipedia article: "a dual-purpose breed", "raised principally for milk production", so dairy is listed first.

Wikipedia article gives the DAD-IS status as "at risk/endangered-maintained" (2026), mapped to endangered-maintained. It also gives FAO (2007) as "critical-maintained" with the figure 66. The DAD-IS record itself could not be opened (the DAD-IS URL returned 404).

facts.v: Its milk is traditionally used for Morlacco del Grappa cheese, which is a Slow Food Presidium.

sources.text: Wikipedia article: milk "traditionally used for Morlacco del Grappa cheese"; the cheese is a Slow Food Praesidium; the breed is listed in Slow Food's Ark of Taste.

facts.v: Traditionally transhumant: cattle graze high alpine pasture in summer and are housed in winter, mostly on hay.
Numbers fell during the World Wars, under the Fascist regime, and through the 1950s and 1960s, largely because the Friesian was seen as more productive.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, on the decline in numbers.

gaps: No milk yield per lactation or lactation length found (the article says only that yield is comparable to other Italian Alpine breeds and about half that of the Frisona Italiana). No fat, protein or casein percentages given. No formation date (origin unknown). Population figures after 2008 not found. The DAD-IS record itself could not be opened; the risk status comes from the Wikipedia article. A thesis's claim of a Jutland origin was not used because the article does not support it.
